terms.gloss: nowhere, in no place; to no place
evidence: Ter. Ad. 4.2.1: frātrem nusquam inveniō gentium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Both “in no place” and, with verbs of motion, “to no place”: nusquam abeō, “I’m not going anywhere” (Ter. Ad. 2.2.38). nusquam gentium is “nowhere on earth”, nusquam alibī “nowhere else”, nusquam nōn “everywhere”. It also means “on no occasion, in nothing”.
Late and rare; the word is nusquam.

phrases.english: I can’t see her anywhere, by Hercules

phrases.latin: potes apparātius cēnāre apud multōs, nusquam hilarius simplicius incautius
phrases.english: you can dine more grandly at many houses, but nowhere more merrily, simply and freely

sources: Lewis & Short: nusquam · Lewis & Short: nullibi
Plautus, Seneca and Pliny from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plautus, loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-plinius); Terence and Cicero as Lewis & Short quotes them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 352.
